stage1.impression: A clear three-beat story told in one flat 'discs' language. A violet meteor strikes, a white cloud bursts into black curls, and the scar it leaves (a four-ring bullseye with the meteor's violet at its centre) becomes the mark, which slides aside into a tidy EARF lockup. The best idea is that the motion builds the logo. The timing undersells it. The first 0.43 s is a held globe with a dot too small to move the trace (0.01-0.16 %, under the 0.2 % line). The hit peaks at 1.0 % (0.47 s), weaker than both the dispersal (1.2 %, 0.73 s) and the layout slide (1.9 %, 1.73 s). The cloud then parks for about 0.15 s. The black crescents read more as claws or crows than as smoke, and they die on a long ease-out tail into a dead stretch before the slide: 0.30 s on paper, 0.40 s on night. On night the crescents vanish once they leave the globe, so the burst looks cropped. Red slivers of the crater peek out of the cloud at 0.60-0.70 s. A faint shockwave arc never finishes fading and is still on the globe in the final lockup at 3.50 s. The end card is a 1.47 s total freeze, 40 % of the runtime. The bullseye and continents depend on colour and will clog at small sizes. A competent draft with a real idea, but not yet a signature.

keep: The motion makes the mark. The violet meteor lodges as the dish's core and the strike leaves the crater, so the ident ends on exactly the logo it just built (frames 03 -> 08 -> 16). That is ownable.

One consistent flat language of discs: the planet, cloud puffs, dish rings and meteor. The ripples are kept to the sea, and the dish's offset rings give depth without a gradient. It reads the same on paper and ink, except for the wisps (change 2).

changes.problem: After the burst, the wisps die on a long, faint fade and then the planet just waits, so the middle of the ident sags. This is the owner's 'not fluid or quick enough'.
changes.evidence: Sheet 1, frames 12-15 (1.20-1.60 s): grey ghost wisps (frame 14, 1.43 s), then a still planet. The trace slides from 0.74 % at 0.83 s to under the 0.2 % line at 1.27 s and stays there until the move at 1.57 s. That is a 0.30 s stop on paper and 0.40 s on ink (sheet 2, 1.17-1.53 s).
changes.expected: The wisps curl out and are gone in about half a second. The move aside starts at 1.19 s (with change 3; 1.27 s on its own) instead of 1.57 s, EARF's wipe ends at 2.04 s, and the ident ends at about 3.34 s instead of 3.72 s. No frame like frame 14, with lingering ghost wisps.

most_important: Change 1: cut wisps.dur from 0.85 to 0.55. The long, faint wisp fade and the 0.3-0.4 s dead stretch before the move are what make the piece feel slow. With the change, the move aside starts at 1.27 s (1.19 s with change 3) instead of 1.57 s, and the ident ends 0.3 s sooner (about 0.4 s with change 3). That answers 'not fluid or quick enough' without touching anything fixed.
out_of_scope: The shared hand-off's 1.3 s hold, plus the wipe's eased tail (under the 0.2 % line from 2.23 s), freezes the last 1.47 s of the ident. That is 40 % of 3.72 s, and about 45 % once the ident is shortened. The lockup is where the brand is read, and a small living detail in the hold (say, one late cone thump) would help. But the hand-off is fixed and shared by every EARF ident, so this is a system decision, not this ident's.

The Planet drawing (fixed) depends on colour: the dish is four concentric fills and the continents are green on blue. At lockup size the violet core is about 3 px on the storyboard (0.04 R) and the rings start to clog. To work in one colour, the identity needs a one-colour rule (dish as rings, land solid, sea knocked out), but the drawing is fixed here.
The meteor's violet is the core's colour (fixed), and on ink (#121114) it has only about 2.7:1 contrast. Changes 8 and 10 help, but colour would be the real fix.
for_owner: Black wisps on ink: we recommend keeping them on the planet (change 2). If you want wisps flying past the planet's edge on ink, they cannot be black there, because they disappear into #121114. They would need the paper colour, on ink only, which bends 'disperses into black wisps'. Your call.
Runtime: the changes take the ident from 3.72 s to about 3.34 s. Please confirm that no placement needs the longer length (the 1.3 s hold is shared and fixed).
The speaker thump (change 5) is a beat you did not ask for. It makes the crater read as a loudspeaker, EARF's product. Please confirm it fits the brand's tone.

'I like how the planet looks in black and white too': do you want a one-colour Planet (print, emboss, single-colour merch) as a deliverable? The ident does not show one, and the fixed drawing would need a one-colour rule.
